newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's TAP says pilots threaten privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's TAP says pilots threaten privatisation.

text.p: State airline TAP-Air Portugal warned its pilots on Tuesday that an eventual strike over working hours could threaten its privatisation and its chances of finding a needed strategic ally.
Company Chairman Manuel Ferreira Lima said such action would also put at risk the company's chances of returning to profit this year for the first time since 1974.
"The conflict with the pilots puts at risk our financial results in 1997, the privatisation and the alliance strategy," he told a news conference to present a new three-year plan.

Ferreira Lima said that a two-day stoppage by the company's 430 pilots would be enough to prevent the company making its target of a 1.3 billion escudo profit this year. Each day of a pilot stoppage would lose 500 million escudos, he said.
The company, which the government hopes to privatise next year or in 1999, lost 10.5 billion escudos in 1996.
TAP pilots and the company are in dispute over the number of extra hours pilots say they are forced to work. The company says that its pilots fly fewer hours than other European airlines.
